A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Router-R1 research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching, including the expanded appendix and renumbered hyperparameter table.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on seven QA datasets, including EM/F1 results, cost trade-offs, unseen-model generalization, and training analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds comparator results, descriptor sensitivity, and training-time routing-pool expansion experiments.

M1.justification: The routing and aggregation procedure, policy objective, reward components, hierarchical format penalty, and cost normalization remain unchanged. The added descriptor and candidate-pool experiments test configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on NQ and HotpotQA and evaluate the same seven general and multi-hop QA datasets. The added experiments vary model descriptors and routing-pool configurations within this retained task coverage.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates FrugalGPT across seven datasets in Table 5; v1 only discussed it as related work. Table 4 also substantially expands the cost comparison with individual routing-pool model rows. The added Mixtral-8x22B row reproduces the retained Largest LLM scores.

E3.justification: Appendices A.2.4–A.2.5 introduce controlled comparisons using compressed descriptors and incorporating LLaMA3-ChatQA-1.5-8B during training. Existing training budgets, evaluation sample sizes, metrics, and main model configurations remain unchanged. The timing of candidate incorporation is unspecified.

E4.justification: V3 adds two substantive robustness investigations absent from v1: sensitivity to descriptor richness and adaptation when a candidate enters the pool during training. These extend the earlier cost-coefficient, format-reward, convergence, test-time generalization, and case-study analyses.

E5.justification: The added experiments introduce no seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting for the retained results is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the shared Table 4 rows retain their numerical values. V3 adds individual-model EM/cost results, FrugalGPT's average EM of 0.318 versus Router-R1-Qwen's 0.416, and averages of 0.419 with compressed descriptors and 0.425 with training-time candidate incorporation. The latter results concern modified experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the appendix cost-normalization definitions are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced; the new normalization caveat is qualitative.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: reinforcement learning for multi-round routing and aggregation, controllable cost–accuracy trade-offs, and generalization to unseen models without retraining. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1.3 newly warns that response-length differences across domains could undermine cost normalization and suggests task-level normalization. A.2.2 expands the cost-frontier interpretation and attributes Mixtral's efficiency to shorter responses; A.2.4–A.2.5 add interpretations concerning descriptor and pool-change robustness.

D1.justification: V3 adds a Hugging Face collection link and an example compressed descriptor. Section 4.3 removes the explicit statement that the implementation was built with Search-R1. Hardware, existing prompts, and hyperparameter values remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and principal related-work discussion are unchanged. However, removing Section 4.3's explicit Search-R1 implementation attribution makes a limited change to the stated relationship with that prior framework.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized grammar corrections, revises cross-references and acknowledgments, shortens redundant discussion, and extends Appendix A with new subsections. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V3 substantially expands the appendix displays through a four-panel cost–performance plot in Figure 5, Tables 5–7, and an individual-model block in Table 4. Existing main figures and table designs are retained; the original hyperparameter Table 5 becomes Table 8.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens the empirical support through FrugalGPT and individual-model comparisons and targeted descriptor and training-pool robustness checks. The normalization caveat also better qualifies applicability. These gains are limited by sparse procedural details and absent uncertainty estimates for the new studies, while removing the explicit Search-R1 implementation attribution modestly weakens provenance. Overall, the additions improve an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
